evidence: Start: [What happened?] Impact window opens at 16:30 UTC on 18 Aug 2022 with certificate-dependent provisioning failures. End: [What happened?] The same window closes at 02:22 UTC the next day. Regions: [What happened?] Provisioning failures are described as occurring globally; no region is named.
notes: Publication date taken from the date shown at the head of the report. regions empty: the report names no region and calls the failures global. services_n counts Azure Key Vault (whose certificate creation was slow) plus Bastion, ExpressRoute, Container Apps, Azure ML, Managed HSM, Confidential VMs, MySQL Flexible Server, PostgreSQL Flexible Server and PostgreSQL Hyperscale.

evidence: Start: [What happened? / What went wrong] A large traffic surge hit the Azure WAN from 08:00 UTC on 29 July 2022, causing drops and latency. End: [How did we respond?] Traffic and packet loss were back to normal by 13:20 UTC, restoring network health for customers. Regions: [What happened?] Fourteen regions are listed as most affected; other regions saw only intermittent cross-WAN impact.
notes: Regions are the fourteen named as most significantly impacted; the report says other unnamed regions may have seen intermittent impact. services_n counts the Azure WAN network connectivity and ExpressRoute, the only products named. Recovery reporting at 15:32 UTC and preventative work to 19:52 UTC are communications and follow-up, not impact.

evidence: Start: [What happened?] New connections and management operations in the region started failing at 03:47 UTC on 21 Jul 2022. End: [What happened? / How did we respond?] Login success telemetry shows failure rates back to normal at 13:30 UTC, despite mitigation first being declared at 18:45. Regions: [What happened?] SQL Database and dependent services in West Europe only.
notes: End is 13:30 UTC, which the report says analysis confirmed as when failure rates returned to pre-incident levels; mitigation was first declared at 18:45 UTC and communicated at 19:16 UTC. The report gives partial recovery at both 06:12 and 06:18 UTC. services_n counts SQL Database, SQL Data Warehouse, App Services, Automation, Backup, Data Factory V2 and Digital Twins.

evidence: Start: [What happened?] Intermittent packet loss from a faulty London WAN router began at 02:40 UTC on 29 June 2022. End: [What happened? / How did we respond?] Impact window ends 20:14 UTC, after engineers pulled the router from service shortly after 20:00. Regions: [What happened?] Traffic to and from UK West, UK South, Europe West and Europe North was affected.
notes: Europe West and Europe North coded as westeurope and northeurope. Failures first seen across 17 regions were later attributed partly to the separate SLB incident (YVTL-RS0); this incident is limited to four regions. services_n counts the Microsoft WAN, ExpressRoute and VPN Gateway.

evidence: Start: [What happened?] Intermittent failures connecting through the Software Load Balancer began at 05:26 UTC on 28 June 2022. End: [What happened?] The stated impact window runs until 04:00 UTC on 1 July 2022. Regions: [What happened? / What went wrong] Impact is given as 14 regions and three regions, none of them named.
notes: scope unclear and regions empty: the report counts 14 and three affected regions but names none. services_n counts Software Load Balancer, Azure Firewall, Private Link, service endpoints, and SQL and Storage (given as examples of services reached through endpoints).

evidence: Start: [What happened?] Customers had trouble reaching resources in one East US 2 availability zone from 02:41 UTC on 07 Jun 2022. End: [What happened? / How did we respond?] Impact window ends at 14:30 UTC, when full mitigation was declared. Regions: [What happened?] One of the three East US 2 zones; zone-redundant services elsewhere in the region stayed up.
notes: zones empty: the report says one of three Availability Zones in East US 2 but gives no zone identifier. Coded zonal because other zones kept serving, though five services (Application Insights, Log Analytics, Managed Identity, Media Services, NetApp Files) and App Service control plane saw regional impact. services_n counts Storage, Virtual Machines, those five services, App Service, ExpressRoute and Spatial Anchors.

evidence: Start: [Summary of impact] Delayed sign-in and audit log data began at 21:35 UTC on 31 May 2022. End: [Summary of impact] The impact window closes at 09:54 UTC on 01 Jun 2022. Regions: [Root Cause] The faulty change reached global endpoints, which the report says impact dependent services globally; no region named.
notes: Scope coded global because the report says the change reached global endpoints whose failure has global impact; it names no region. services_n counts Azure Active Directory logging, Microsoft Graph, Azure portal, Application Insights, Log Analytics, PowerShell and Azure Resource Manager.

evidence: Start: [Summary of Impact] ARM management operation errors in Azure Government began at 11:49 EST on 01 March 2022. End: [Summary of Impact] Errors ended at 03:08 EST on 03 Mar 2022. Regions: [Summary of Impact] Only the Azure Government cloud is named, with no region.
notes: This report states times in EST, not UTC; converted with UTC-5 (standard time in effect, before the 13 Mar 2022 change). scope unclear and regions empty: only the Azure Government cloud is named, no region. services_n counts Azure Resource Manager.

evidence: Start: [Summary of Impact] Database unavailability on one hardware generation began at 11:45 UTC on 12 Feb 2022. End: [Summary of Impact] The stated window ends at 11:43 UTC on 15 Feb 2022. Regions: [Summary of Impact] Affected hardware sat in six regions, which are not named.
notes: scope unclear and regions empty: six regions are counted but not named. The Mitigation section says most databases recovered earlier, with the fix rollout finishing 14 Feb for Cosmos DB and 15 Feb for SQL DB; no earlier end time is given. services_n counts SQL Database and Cosmos DB.

evidence: Start: [Impact Statement] Connection failures to some West US resources began at 04:38 UTC on 12 Feb 2022. End: [Impact Statement] The impact window closes at 06:30 UTC the same day. Regions: [Impact Statement] Only resources hosted in West US are described as affected.
notes: Report gives a preliminary root cause only. services_n counts Virtual Machines, Azure SQL and Storage; unnamed downstream services are not counted. No zone named; the whole-region scope is the report's wording.
